claims.text: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films and nanoribbons have high defect densities.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films and nanoribbons contain substantial residual stress.
The nanocrystalline microstructure of deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type films differs from that of bulk-cast counterparts.
Rapid thermal annealing at 400–500 °C for a few minutes in an inert atmosphere can partially relieve internal stress.
The proposed annealing window can modify grain-boundary conditions without causing unwanted grain growth or phase segregation.
Annealing reduces residual strain and defect density in the nanoscale alloy.
Changes in residual strain, defects, and grain structure mediate magnetostructural transformation kinetics.
Changes in residual strain, defects, and grain structure affect domain-wall mobility.
Relaxing internal stress and reducing defect-induced pinning makes the magnetostructural transition more uniform and reversible.
A more uniform and reversible magnetostructural transition reduces thermal hysteresis.
Annealing shifts the effective magnetostructural transition temperature.
The transition-temperature shift is likely upward because annealing improves thermal equilibrium.
Reducing the number of nucleation sites lowers latent heat and therefore modestly lowers the peak magnetocaloric response.
Annealed samples will have narrower magnetic hysteresis than as-deposited samples during low-field cycles.
As-deposited nanoscale films and nanoribbons exhibit significant hysteresis under low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
As-deposited nanoscale samples retain a relatively high latent-heat-related magnetocaloric response, although the bulk response may not fully persist.
Heat-transfer limitations constrain cycle frequency in sub-100-nm films or patterned nanoribbons.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says annealing will 'refine' the grain structure, while the mediator predicts slight coarsening and the intervention is intended to avoid unwanted grain growth. The intended direction and acceptable extent of the grain-size change are therefore ambiguous.

The predicted outcome compares the reduced magnetocaloric peak primarily with a bulk-like response, whereas the falsification rule requires reduction relative to the as-deposited baseline. These are different comparators.
